q: The compounds formed by the combination of two elements are called _____ compounds.
e: The compounds formed by the combination of two elements are called binary compounds. Binary is the idea that completes this fact. Ternary would fill a different blank than binary.

q: The compounds formed by the combination of three elements are called _____ compounds.
e: The compounds formed by the combination of three elements are called ternary compounds. Ternary is the idea that completes this fact. Binary would fill a different blank than ternary.

q: A heterogeneous mixture is one that is non-uniform, and where the different components of the mixture can be _____.
e: A heterogeneous mixture is one that is non-uniform, and where the different components of the mixture can be seen. Seen is the idea that completes this fact. Dissolved would fill a different blank than seen.

q: A homogeneous mixture is one in which the composition of its components are _____ mixed throughout.
e: A homogeneous mixture is one in which the composition of its components are uniformly mixed throughout. Uniformly is the idea that completes this fact. Randomly would fill a different blank than uniformly.

q: An alloy is a substance made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to _____.
e: An alloy is a substance made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion. Corrosion is the idea that completes this fact. Heat would fill a different blank than corrosion.

q: Magnetic separation is used to separate the components of a mixture when at least one of them is _____ in nature.
e: Magnetic separation is used to separate the components of a mixture when at least one of them is magnetic in nature. Magnetic is the idea that completes this fact. Radioactive would fill a different blank than magnetic.

q: Some solids such as sand, charcoal and chalk are _____ in water.
e: Some solids such as sand, charcoal and chalk are insoluble in water. Insoluble is the idea that completes this fact. Soluble would fill a different blank than insoluble.

q: Some liquids can mix with one another in all proportions and are called _____ liquids.
e: Some liquids can mix with one another in all proportions and are called miscible liquids. Miscible is the idea that completes this fact. Immiscible would fill a different blank than miscible.

q: Liquids that do not mix are called _____ liquids.
e: Liquids that do not mix are called immiscible liquids. Immiscible is the idea that completes this fact. Miscible is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Dry air is a familiar example of a _____ solution.
e: Dry air is a familiar example of a gaseous solution. Gaseous is the idea that completes this fact. Liquid would fill a different blank than gaseous.

q: Brass is an example of a _____ solution.
e: Brass is an example of a solid solution. Solid is the idea that completes this fact. Gaseous would fill a different blank than solid.

q: Salt water is a familiar example of a solid dissolved within a _____.
e: Salt water is a familiar example of a solid dissolved within a liquid. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact. Solid would fill a different blank than liquid.

q: Carbonated water contains carbon dioxide gas molecules existing between molecules of _____.
e: Carbonated water contains carbon dioxide gas molecules existing between molecules of water. Water is the idea that completes this fact. Ethanol would fill a different blank than water.

q: Blood and saliva are some of the more familiar solutions of _____ importance.
e: Blood and saliva are some of the more familiar solutions of biological importance. Biological is the idea that completes this fact. Physical would fill a different blank than biological.

q: A solution is a _____ mixture of two or more substances.
e: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances. A homogeneous mixture looks the same throughout, like a clear solution. Heterogeneous would fill a different blank than homogeneous.

q: When sugar is mixed with water, the sugar is the _____ and water is the solvent.
e: When sugar is mixed with water, the sugar is the solute and water is the solvent. The solute is the substance that dissolves. Mixture would fill a different blank than solute.

q: Solutions having water as the solvent are referred to as _____ solutions.
e: Solutions having water as the solvent are referred to as aqueous solutions. Aqueous is the idea that completes this fact. Liquid would fill a different blank than aqueous.

q: If some more solid added can dissolve with stirring, this solution is known as an _____ solution.
e: If some more solid added can dissolve with stirring, this solution is known as an unsaturated solution. Unsaturated is the idea that completes this fact. Supersaturated would fill a different blank than unsaturated.

q: A _____ solution forms when no more solute can be dissolved in the given amount of solvent at that temperature even if it is stirred.
e: A saturated solution forms when no more solute can be dissolved in the given amount of solvent at that temperature even if it is stirred. Saturated is the idea that completes this fact. Supersaturated would fill a different blank than saturated.

q: The amount in grams of the solute in 100 g of water to give a saturated solution at that experimental temperature is known as the _____ of that solute.
e: The amount in grams of the solute in 100 g of water to give a saturated solution at that experimental temperature is known as the solubility of that solute. Solubility is the idea that completes this fact. Concentration would fill a different blank than solubility.

q: If the solution contains more solute than it should have at room temperature, it is a _____ solution.
e: If the solution contains more solute than it should have at room temperature, it is a supersaturated solution. Supersaturated is the idea that completes this fact. Saturated would fill a different blank than supersaturated.

q: When the temperature of the solution is increased, the solubility of most solutes _____.
e: When the temperature of the solution is increased, the solubility of most solutes increases. Increases is the idea that completes this fact. Decreases would fill a different blank than increases.

q: The solubility of all gases and some solids such as calcium hydroxide and calcium sulphate _____ when temperature of the solution is increased.
e: The solubility of all gases and some solids such as calcium hydroxide and calcium sulphate decreases when temperature of the solution is increased. Decreases is the idea that completes this fact. Increases would fill a different blank than decreases.

q: In a solution, the solute is _____ distributed throughout the solution.
e: In a solution, the solute is uniformly distributed throughout the solution. Uniformly is the idea that completes this fact. Unevenly would fill a different blank than uniformly.

q: A solvent is a substance, mostly liquid, in which another substance dissolves to give a _____ mixture.
e: A solvent is a substance, mostly liquid, in which another substance dissolves to give a homogeneous mixture. A homogeneous mixture looks the same throughout, like a clear solution. Heterogeneous would fill a different blank than homogeneous.

q: The ocean is a vast water solution containing different compounds extracted from the minerals of the Earth's _____.
e: The ocean is a vast water solution containing different compounds extracted from the minerals of the Earth's crust. Crust is the idea that completes this fact. Core would fill a different blank than crust.

q: Nutrients are carried in water solution to all parts of a _____.
e: Nutrients are carried in water solution to all parts of a plant. Plant is the idea that completes this fact. Mineral would fill a different blank than plant.

q: Ethanol, acetic acid and sulphuric acid are _____ in water.
e: Ethanol, acetic acid and sulphuric acid are soluble in water. Soluble is the idea that completes this fact. Immiscible would fill a different blank than soluble.

q: Petrol and oils are _____ in water.
e: Petrol and oils are insoluble in water. Insoluble is the idea that completes this fact. Soluble would fill a different blank than insoluble.

q: Hydrogen chloride and ammonia are gases that are _____ in water.
e: Hydrogen chloride and ammonia are gases that are soluble in water. Soluble is the idea that completes this fact. Immiscible would fill a different blank than soluble.

q: Oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen are gases that are not very _____ in water.
e: Oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen are gases that are not very soluble in water. Soluble is the idea that completes this fact. Immiscible is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Solubility of a substance at a given temperature is the mass in grams of the substance which will saturate _____ g of water, at that temperature.
e: Solubility of a substance at a given temperature is the mass in grams of the substance which will saturate 100 g of water, at that temperature. 100 is the idea that completes this fact. 10 would fill a different blank than 100.

q: A solution in which more of the solute can dissolve at the given temperature is called an _____ solution.
e: A solution in which more of the solute can dissolve at the given temperature is called an unsaturated solution. Unsaturated is the idea that completes this fact. Supersaturated would fill a different blank than unsaturated.

q: The solution that retains more solute than that required to saturate the solution at room temperature is called a _____ solution.
e: The solution that retains more solute than that required to saturate the solution at room temperature is called a supersaturated solution. Supersaturated is the idea that completes this fact. Unsaturated would fill a different blank than supersaturated.

q: When a saturated solution at a higher temperature is cooled, the solubility decreases, so the excess solute will come out as a _____.
e: When a saturated solution at a higher temperature is cooled, the solubility decreases, so the excess solute will come out as a solid. Solid is the idea that completes this fact. Gas would fill a different blank than solid.

q: Wine is separated from the sediments by _____ in daily life applications.
e: Wine is separated from the sediments by decantation in daily life applications. Decantation is the idea that completes this fact. Filtration would fill a different blank than decantation.

q: Plasma can be removed from blood by decantation after _____.
e: Plasma can be removed from blood by decantation after centrifugation. Centrifugation is the idea that completes this fact. Filtration would fill a different blank than centrifugation.

q: Milk is a colloid of fat globules suspended in water, which is an example of a _____ mixture.
e: Milk is a colloid of fat globules suspended in water, which is an example of a heterogeneous mixture. A heterogeneous mixture has visibly different parts. Pure would fill a different blank than heterogeneous.

q: Decanting a mixture containing flammable solvents can be dangerous as the flammable material evaporates and forms dangerous _____.
e: Decanting a mixture containing flammable solvents can be dangerous as the flammable material evaporates and forms dangerous fumes. Fumes is the idea that completes this fact. Solids would fill a different blank than fumes.
